findings.reason: a worker applying the constant as stated drops figure rows from the metadata index and changes the discovery change signature, a regression that none of §2's six cases or two negative controls exercises because they never place a figure in the tree.
findings.text: §2 makes `covered_name` and the covered walk read `resources.INFRA_DIRS` and stop descending into those directories, but that constant contains `figures` (reckon/resources.py:39-48) while the covered set is defined as every HTML file plus the figure images under the top-level figures directory (`_FIGURE_DIR = "figures"`, reckon/metadata_index.py:80, and `covered_name` at :362-375), so the rule as written removes `docs/figures/**` from the covered set and from discovery's counted set

findings.reason: the deliverable must name the worker-thread callable as the scope entry point (or copy the context into the executor call), otherwise the boundary has no effect and the node only discovers it after its gate fails.
findings.text: §2 says `mcp_deadlines._deadline_tool` "enters `discovery_file_scope` and `resource_scan_scope` once around the tool body", but that wrapper runs every body on a worker thread via `loop.run_in_executor` (reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:365-367, `_run_under_deadline` at :438-449), and both scopes are ContextVar-based (metadata_index.py:100-120, resources.py:507-535); `run_in_executor` does not copy the context, so a scope opened in the async entry is empty inside the body (reproduced: a ContextVar set before `run_in_executor` reads its default in the body, while `asyncio.to_thread` reads the set value)

findings.reason: a coordinator or worker reading the followup dispatches §5 in parallel with §2 against a declared dependency and plans work for a §4 that will never be built.
findings.text: followup f-arcwc-001 still reads "§2 and §5 start at once; §3 and §4 follow §2; §6 follows §2, §3 and work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop §19; §7 follows all five", while `plan-section-depends-on` now descopes s4 (folded into §2), adds s5 → s3, and leaves s7 with s2, s3, s5 and s6
